Issues.Title: Tailwind 4.3.3 changes the default sans font in a patch release
Issues.Body:
Upgrading Tailwind from 4.3.2 to 4.3.3 changed our application’s typography and text metrics.

The default changed from:

ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

to:

-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", "Noto Sans", Arial, sans-serif

This was intended to fix CJK language handling on Windows, but also changes Latin typography, wrapping, and layout depending on locally installed fonts.

The change is documented under “Fixed” in the 4.3.3 release notes (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/releases/tag/v4.3.3), despite being visually breaking. The font-family documentation (https://tailwindcss.com/docs/font-family) still shows the previous default stack.

Tailwind previously stated that Preflight follows semantic versioning and should not change incompatibly within a major version in this maintainer discussion (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/7496). Shipping a global typography change in a patch release appears inconsistent with that expectation.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Tailwind 4.3.3 changes the default sans font in a patch release" (#20348)

Issues.Title: Ensure `@source` files behind symlinks trigger rebuilds in `@tailwindcss/vite`
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20346

## Summary

Since #20203 the scanner preserves symlinks in `@source` paths, so `scanner.files` can contain a path like `app/node_modules/pkg/index.js` while Vite tracks the module and its file change events under the real `packages/pkg/index.js`. The plugin registered only the written path via `addWatchFile`, which Vite's watcher ignores inside `node_modules`, so editing the real file behind a workspace symlink never invalidated the CSS module and new candidates only appeared after restarting the dev server.

This registers the resolved path alongside the written one for scanned files and glob bases, cached per root. `isScannedFile` gets the missing direction too: it already resolved the changed file before comparing against scanned paths, now it also resolves scanned paths before comparing against the changed file, so full reloads for non-module `@source` files keep working when the path goes through a symlink.

## Test plan

Added an integration test with a pnpm workspace where `@source` points through the `node_modules` symlink of a linked workspace package. It fails without the change (the new candidate never appears until the dev server restarts) and passes with it. The full `integrations/vite` suite passes. Also verified the reproduction from #20346 directly: with this build, editing the file behind the symlink updates the page without a restart.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Ensure `@source` files behind symlinks trigger rebuilds in `@tailwindcss/vite`" (#20347)

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/vite does not hot-reload new candidates from explicit @source files behind workspace symlinks since v4.3.1
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3

This regressed between v4.3.0 and v4.3.1 and is still reproducible in v4.3.3.

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

Vite 8.1.4 with @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3 and a pnpm workspace.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v24.18.0

**What browser are you using?**

N/A 

**What operating system are you using?**

Linux 6.18.38 x86_64

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/ageorgeh/tailwind-vite-symlink-hmr-reproduction

**Describe your issue**

When an explicit `@source` points to a file through a pnpm workspace symlink, Tailwind scans the file correctly at startup, but changes to the real source file do not trigger a rescan.

Steps:

1. Run `pnpm install`.
2. Run `pnpm dev`.
3. Open the displayed URL and confirm the example text is red.
4. Without stopping Vite, change `text-red-500` to `text-green-500` in `packages/repro-package/source.html`.
5. Click “Use text-green-500” in the browser.

Expected: Tailwind detects the new candidate, regenerates the CSS, and the text becomes green.

Actual: `.text-green-500` is not generated and the text is unstyled. Restarting Vite causes the class to be generated.

Changing both `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/vite` to v4.3.0 makes the update work without restarting Vite.

This appears related to #20203. 

LLM reasoning as to why: Before that change, source optimization canonicalized the complete source path, including symlinked path segments. Since v4.3.1, the scanner preserves the symlink path. `@tailwindcss/vite` then passes paths from `scanner.files` to `addWatchFile`, but edits happen at the symlink's real workspace target. No watcher update reaches Tailwind, so the file is never rescanned.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "@tailwindcss/vite does not hot-reload new candidates from explicit @source files behind workspace symlinks since v4.3.1" (#20346)

Issues.Title: Fix changes to symlinked files outside of the project works
Issues.Body: This PR fixes an issue where changes to a symlinked file wouldn't result in hot-reload when using `@tailwincdss/vite`. This issue also exists in the other packages such as `@tailwincdss/postcss`, `@tailwincdss/webpack` and `@tailwincdss/cli`. The issue is that we watch the symlinked file, but not the "real" file for changes. If the source of the symlinked file lives in another folder that is not covered by auto-source detection or by any of the `@source` directives, then changes to that file won't trigger a change. To solve this, if a file is symlinked or lives in a symlinked folder, then we will make sure that the `scanner.files` contains the real path / canonicalized path to the real file as well just so we can detect changes in that file. Fixes: #20346 Closes: #20347 ## Test plan 1. Added a regression test for `@tailwindcss/vite` 2. Added tests in the scanner code itself 3. Manually tested on the reproduction: |   | Initial state | After change | | ---: | --- | --- | | **Before** | | | | **After** | | | [ci-all]

Issues.Title: Fix failing upgrade test in CI
Issues.Body:
The last CI run on `main` was on July 16, and the last `globby` release (16.2.2) was released on July 15 (~21 hours earlier). Due to the default `minimumReleaseAge` in pnpm of 24 hours, it meant that we were receiving the previous globby version.

In the new version, they slightly changed some of the `.gitignore` parsing, but in one of our upgrade tests we wrote an invalid `.gitignore` file (which had indented lines). 

This PR fixes that by using the `txt` tagged template literal, which behind the scenes uses `dedent` which in turn makes sure that we ship a proper `.gitignore` file.


## Test plan

All tests should pass [ci-all]

Issues.Title: Invalid code point 6685633 in String.fromCodePoint on oxide-linux-x64-gnu@4.1.18 (works on 4.3.2)
Issues.Body:
## Bug report — `Invalid code point 6685633` in `String.fromCodePoint` on `oxide-linux-x64-gnu@4.1.18`

### Summary

`vite build` fails deterministically with `Invalid code point 6685633` on Linux x86_64 when using `tailwindcss@4.1.18` + `@tailwindcss/vite@4.1.18`. Same setup works on Windows (`oxide-win32-x64-msvc@4.1.18`). Upgrading to `4.3.2` resolves the issue.

### Reproduction

**Environment**: `node:20-alpine` Docker image (any recent Linux distro reproduces).

**Minimal repro** — no application code required:

```bash
mkdir tw-repro && cd tw-repro
npm init -y
npm i -D tailwindcss@4.1.18 @tailwindcss/vite@4.1.18 vite@7 laravel-vite-plugin
mkdir -p resources/css
echo "@import 'tailwindcss';" > resources/css/app.css
cat > vite.config.js <<'EOF'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import laravel from 'laravel-vite-plugin';
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';

export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [
        laravel({ input: ['resources/css/app.css'], refresh: false }),
        tailwindcss(),
    ],
});
EOF
npx vite build
```

### Expected

Build succeeds and outputs a compiled CSS file.

### Actual

```
vite v7.3.6 building client environment for production...
transforming...
✓ 0 modules transformed.
✗ Build failed in 2m 44s
error during build:
[@tailwindcss/vite:generate:build] Invalid code point 6685633
file: <repo>/resources/css/app.css
    at Function.fromCodePoint (<anonymous>)
    at file://<repo>/node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/chunk-CT46QCH7.mjs:1:5453
    at String.replace (<anonymous>)
    at Se (file://<repo>/node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/chunk-CT46QCH7.mjs:1:5382)
    at lt.markUsedVariable (file://<repo>/node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/chunk-CT46QCH7.mjs:1:7620)
    at Object.build (file://<repo>/node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/chunk-CT46QCH7.mjs:38:1073)
    at Object.build (file://<repo>/node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/chunk-CT46QCH7.mjs:38:1457)
    at F.generate (file://<repo>/node_modules/@tailwindcss/vite/dist/index.mjs:1:5719)
    at async Object.handler (file://<repo>/node_modules/@tailwindcss/vite/dist/index.mjs:1:3118)
```

The code point `6685633` (`0x660801`) is above `0x10FFFF` (the max Unicode codepoint), so `String.fromCodePoint` throws.

### Analysis

- Fully deterministic — reproduced 4 times on independent runs.
- Reproducible with `resources/css/app.css` containing **only** `@import 'tailwindcss';` — no `@source`, no `@theme`, no custom CSS, no scanned templates involved.
- Platform-dependent:
  - `@tailwindcss/oxide-win32-x64-msvc@4.1.18` — works fine.
  - `@tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu@4.1.18` — fails systematically.
- Comes from `markUsedVariable` in the Rust `oxide` binary, which appears to be passing a corrupt 32-bit integer into `String.fromCodePoint` on the JS side.

### Version matrix

| tailwindcss | oxide-linux-x64-gnu | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `4.1.18` | `4.1.18` | ❌ crashes with `Invalid code point 6685633` |
| `4.3.2` | `4.3.2` | ✅ builds successfully |

`4.3.2` was validated with the same minimal reproduction and with a full production build (multiple entry points + `@source` scanning ~700 Blade + JS files) — both pass in `2m 13s` and `2m 3s` respectively.

### Environment details

- **OS**: Linux x86_64 (Docker `node:20-alpine`)
- **Node**: `v20.20.2`
- **npm**: `10.8.2`
- **Vite**: `7.3.6`
- **Framework**: Laravel Vite plugin `2.0.0`
- **Failing versions**: `tailwindcss@4.1.18`, `@tailwindcss/vite@4.1.18`, `@tailwindcss/oxide@4.1.18`
- **Working versions**: `tailwindcss@4.3.2`, `@tailwindcss/vite@4.3.2`, `@tailwindcss/oxide@4.3.2`
- Windows equivalent (`oxide-win32-x64-msvc@4.1.18`): not affected.

### Workaround

Upgrade to `4.3.2`+ (any `4.3.x` version we could test resolves the issue).

### Note

This bug blocks CI pipelines pinned to `4.1.18`. Reporting for tracking / patch release of `4.1.x` line if that line is still supported.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Invalid code point 6685633 in String.fromCodePoint on oxide-linux-x64-gnu@4.1.18 (works on 4.3.2)" (#20354)

Issues.Title: cssConflict lint rule flags false positives on mutually exclusive data attributes after v4.3.3
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please provide all of the information requested below. We're a small team and without all of this information it's not possible for us to help and your bug report will be closed. -->

**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3 (The issue does not occur in v4.3.2)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

Vite 8.1.5, @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, Svelte 5.56.6

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

Bun 1.3.14 (Node.js compatible environment)

**What browser are you using?**

N/A (Editor / Linting issue)

**What operating system are you using?**

Windows

**Reproduction URL**

Since this is an editor-linting/language-server issue (Tailwind CSS IntelliSense), it is difficult to reproduce in Tailwind Play. 

However, you can easily reproduce this locally in VS Code with a fresh project using Tailwind CSS v4.3.3:

1. Define a custom variant in your CSS:
```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@custom-variant is-hocus (&:is(:hover, :focus-visible));
```

2. Write the following classes in a JS/TS file:
```typescript
const className = "data-[state=on]:is-hocus:bg-red-500 data-[state=off]:is-hocus:bg-blue-500";
```

3. In VS Code, the Tailwind CSS IntelliSense extension will trigger a `cssConflict` warning:
`'data-[state=on]:is-hocus:bg-red-500' applies the same CSS properties as 'data-[state=off]:is-hocus:bg-blue-500'.`

*(This warning is not shown when downgraded to v4.3.2)*

**Describe your issue**

After upgrading from v4.3.2 to v4.3.3, the Tailwind CSS IntelliSense linting rules (specifically `cssConflict`) started throwing false positive warnings on mutually exclusive variant conditions.

For example, `data-[state=on]` and `data-[state=off]` are mutually exclusive states that can never be active at the same time. Therefore, combining `data-[state=on]:is-hocus:bg-...` and `data-[state=off]:is-hocus:bg-...` in the same element will never cause a CSS property clash.

However, the linter flags this as a CSS conflict warning because it only looks at the base utility (both are modifying `background-color` under `is-hocus`) and does not recognize that the underlying `data-` attributes are exclusive.

We suspect this behavior started appearing due to the selector parsing bug fix in v4.3.3 (**#20303**: *Parse selectors like [data-foo]div as two selectors instead of one*). The parser is now able to properly parse these complex nested selectors, but as a side effect, it exposes them to the naive `cssConflict` check which cannot handle exclusive conditions.

Similar false positives are now occurring for:
- `group-data-minimized:hidden` and `group-data-maximized:hidden`
- `animate-pulse` and `data-[type=error]:animate-spin`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "cssConflict lint rule flags false positives on mutually exclusive data attributes after v4.3.3" (#20345)

Issues.Title: Ensure `drop-shadow-*` utilities work with theme values containing multiple shadows
Issues.Body:
Fixes #17677

## Summary

Theme values for `drop-shadow-*` that contain multiple shadows currently produce broken CSS unless the user remembers to declare them with `@theme inline`. Given:

```css
@theme {
  --drop-shadow-multi: 0 0 20px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2), 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25);
}
```

`drop-shadow-multi` generates:

```css
--tw-drop-shadow: drop-shadow(var(--drop-shadow-multi));
```

which is invalid because the comma-separated list ends up inside a single `drop-shadow(…)` function — each shadow needs its own `drop-shadow(…)` wrapper (the sibling `--tw-drop-shadow-size` declaration already does this correctly).

This PR implements the approach suggested in the issue discussion: when a `--drop-shadow-*` theme value contains multiple shadows, treat it as if it were declared with `@theme inline`, since a single `var(…)` reference can never represent it correctly. The output for the theme value above becomes:

```css
--tw-drop-shadow: drop-shadow(0 0 20px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)) drop-shadow(0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25));
```

Single-shadow theme values are unaffected and keep referencing the variable, so overriding them via the cascade continues to work.

## Test plan

- Added a non-inline multi-shadow theme value (`--drop-shadow-double`) to the existing `filter` test in `utilities.test.ts`. It now compiles to the same (valid) output as the `@theme inline` variant — previously it produced the broken single-`drop-shadow(…)` output described above.
- `pnpm vitest run --project tailwindcss` — all 4871 tests pass.
- Verified the reproduction from #17677 produces valid CSS after the change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Ensure `drop-shadow-*` utilities work with theme values containing multiple shadows" (#20337)

Issues.Title: Don't trigger a full page reload for scanned files that Vite processes as modules
Issues.Body: This PR fixes an issue where editing a scanned file that Vite (or one of its plugins) can process as a module, but that isn't currently loaded, caused `@tailwindcss/vite` to force a full page reload, throwing away all client state. The `hotUpdate` hook has a fallback that sends a `full-reload` for files that Tailwind scans but that Vite knows nothing about (e.g. `.php` or `.blade.php` templates rendered by a backend). Without it, edits to those files wouldn't refresh the page at all. To detect those files we check whether every module for the changed file is an `asset` and/or has no id, because the scanner's `addWatchFile` calls create exactly such placeholder nodes for every scanned file. The problem is that a source file that Vite _can_ process, but that isn't loaded yet, looks exactly the same. The realistic way to get into that state is code splitting: with route-level splitting (e.g. `React.lazy`, TanStack Router's `autoCodeSplitting`, lazy routes in `vue-router`), every component behind an un-visited split boundary only exists as a scan placeholder in the module graph. Editing any of them reloaded the whole app. The same happens for component stylesheets that a framework plugin compiles into the component (e.g. Angular via Analog), which never show up as their own module. A full reload is never useful for these files: if the file is loaded, Vite's own HMR handles it, and if it isn't loaded, reloading the page won't load it either. Any new candidates still apply through the regular `css-update` flow because the file is registered via `addWatchFile`. So instead, we now skip the fallback when the changed file is handled by Vite's module pipeline: - The file exists as a real module in another environment (e.g. an SSR-only module). This check already existed and is folded into the same code path. - The file is part of the JS/TS or CSS families, which Vite transforms natively. - For any other file type (e.g. `.vue`, `.svelte`, or `.md` with an SSG plugin), a file with the same extension exists as a real module in some environment's module graph, then a plugin does handle this file type and the changed file just isn't loaded (yet). External templates like `.php` files still trigger a full reload exactly like before. Fixes: #20320 Fixes: #19903 Closes: #20323 ## Test plan 1. Added integration tests to ensure extensions handled by default rely on HMR 2. Added integration tests to make sure that unknown extensions that have been handled already will also use HMR 3. Manually tested that changing a `.php` file still triggers a `full-reload` 4. Manually tested the reproduction where local client state isn't thrown away
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Don't trigger a full page reload for scanned files that Vite processes as modules" (#20336)

Issues.Title: Root-level concrete @source hides nested concrete sources with source(none) in v4.3.2
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?** v4.3.2 **What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?** Vite 8.1.4 with @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.2 **What version of Node.js are you using?** For example: v20.0.0 **What browser are you using?** N/A **What operating system are you using?** Linux **Reproduction URL** https://github.com/ageorgeh/tailwind-concrete-source-regression **Describe your issue** This appears to be a regression from Tailwind CSS 4.3.1 to 4.3.2. With automatic source detection disabled, an imported CSS file declares a nested concrete source followed by a root-level concrete source: /* input.css */ @import "tailwindcss" source(none); @import "./component-sources.css"; /* component-sources.css */ @source "./nested/component.html"; @source "./component-sources.classes.txt"; The source files contain separate classes:
/* component-sources.classes.txt */ bg-red-500 To reproduce: npm ci npm run verify Under 4.3.2, the root-level class is generated, but the class from the nested concrete source is missing: bg-red-500: present text-green-500: missing I expected both classes to be present in the generated CSS. The repository includes a works-v4.3.1 tag containing the same project with tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite pinned to 4.3.1: git checkout works-v4.3.1 npm ci npm run verify Both classes are generated under 4.3.1.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Root-level concrete @source hides nested concrete sources with source(none) in v4.3.2" (#20333)

Issues.Title: `@tailwindcss/upgrade` rewrites files in `node_modules` when run from a pnpm workspace subpackage
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When `@tailwindcss/upgrade` is run from a **subpackage of a pnpm workspace**, it traverses `../../node_modules/…` and rewrites files inside the installed `tailwindcss` package in place — applying its v3 → v4 migration transform (`@tailwind utilities;` → `@import 'tailwindcss/utilities' layer(utilities);`) to `node_modules/tailwindcss/utilities.css` (and, in a flat-project variant, to `index.css`).

This looks like the tail of [#19726](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/19726) — the fix landed there (ignore gitignored files) works for the simple flat-project case, but doesn't cover the workspace-subpackage variant where the tool reaches `node_modules` through `../../`. In our case (a pnpm-workspace v4 project), running the tool as a canonicalizer left `node_modules/tailwindcss/utilities.css` self-referentially importing itself, which detonated much later as an infinite CSS-resolution loop and read like a "cache corruption" problem.

## Reproduction

Repo: https://github.com/benface/tailwindcss-upgrade-node-modules-repro

```sh
git clone https://github.com/benface/tailwindcss-upgrade-node-modules-repro
cd tailwindcss-upgrade-node-modules-repro
pnpm install
cd packages/css
pnpm dlx @tailwindcss/upgrade
```

The tool's own output confirms the write:

```
│ ↳ Migrated stylesheet: `../../node_modules/.pnpm/tailwindcss@4.3.2/node_modules/tailwindcss/utilities.css`
│ ↳ Updated package: `tailwindcss`
```

Diff against a pristine copy from the tarball:

```diff
1c1
< @tailwind utilities;
---
> @import 'tailwindcss/utilities' layer(utilities);
```

`node_modules` is gitignored at the repo root (and even at the subpackage level, tested separately — same result).

## Counter-tests (where the existing fix works correctly)

For contrast, both of these leave `node_modules` untouched:

- Flat project (no workspace), `node_modules` in `.gitignore`, `@import 'tailwindcss'`, run from project root
- Same, using explicit-path imports (`@import 'tailwindcss/utilities.css' layer(utilities) source(none)`)

The pnpm-workspace-subpackage layout is the specific gap.

## Why this matters

1. **`node_modules` shouldn't be a write target.** The files are shared across projects via the pnpm store, are immutable install artifacts elsewhere, and are out of scope for `git status`, so the corruption is invisible until it detonates.
2. **The rewrite creates a self-referential import** — the mutated `utilities.css` imports itself under a `layer(...)` wrapper, causing an infinite CSS-resolution loop.
3. **Symptoms look unrelated to the upgrade run** — the user hits infinite-recursion errors much later, from any command that touches Tailwind, with a clean `git status`.
4. **Recovery requires nuking `node_modules` + reinstalling** (and on Bun, purging the install cache too, per #19726). Not obvious from the symptoms.

## Suggested guard

Skip any file whose resolved absolute path falls under a `node_modules/` segment, regardless of how it was reached (traversal via `../../`, symlink resolution, or `@import` resolution). The existing gitignore-aware filter probably just needs its input paths canonicalized before the check.

## Environment

- macOS (arm64), Node 24, pnpm 11.12.0
- `tailwindcss@4.3.2`
- `@tailwindcss/upgrade@4.3.2` (via `pnpm dlx`)

Happy to test a fix.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "`@tailwindcss/upgrade` rewrites files in `node_modules` when run from a pnpm workspace subpackage" (#20328)

Issues.Title: Prevent `@tailwindcss/upgrade` from rewriting files inside `node_modules` when run from a workspace subpackage
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20328.

## What changed

When `@tailwindcss/upgrade` is invoked from a subpackage of a workspace (e.g. `pnpm --filter …` or `cd packages/foo && pnpm exec upgrade`), it traverses `../../node_modules/…` and applies its v3 → v4 migration transform (`@tailwind utilities;` → `@import 'tailwindcss/utilities' layer(utilities);`) to files inside the installed `tailwindcss` package itself — a self-referential import that later detonates as an infinite CSS-resolution loop and reads like a "cache corruption" bug (matches the report in #19726 / #20328).

Root cause: `globby`'s `isGitIgnored` only walks `.gitignore` files at or below its `cwd`. When invoked from a subpackage, the workspace-root `.gitignore` (which almost always lists `node_modules`) is never consulted, and `../../node_modules/…` paths come back as **not** ignored.

The fix anchors `isGitIgnored` at the git repository root instead of the subpackage:

- New helper: `gitRoot(cwd)` in `src/utils/git.ts` — thin wrapper over `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
- `analyze(stylesheets, { base })` in `src/codemods/css/analyze.ts` now calls `isGitIgnored({ cwd: gitRoot(base) ?? base })`. Falls back to the previous behavior when not inside a git repository or when `git` is unavailable.

## Test

Added an integration test that reproduces the exact scenario: a pnpm workspace with a subpackage that imports `tailwindcss/utilities.css`, upgrade run from the subpackage, then asserts `packages/css/node_modules/tailwindcss/utilities.css` still holds the pristine `@tailwind utilities;` directive.

Verified the test fails on `main` and passes with this change.

The 415 existing upgrade unit tests still pass. Two npm-related snapshot failures in `upgrade-errors.test.ts` (`half-upgraded v3 project to v4 (bun|npm)`) pre-exist this change — they're about newer npm's `npm notice run` output that isn't in the snapshots, unrelated to what this PR touches.


---

Edit by @RobinMalfait: going to run on all [ci-all] so we can make sure it works on Windows as well.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Prevent `@tailwindcss/upgrade` from rewriting files inside `node_modules` when run from a workspace subpackage" (#20329)

Issues.Title: [Bug]: @tailwindcss/webpack fully rescans sources on every one-file HMR rebuild
Issues.Body:
### Summary

`@tailwindcss/webpack` performs a full `scanner.scan()` on every incremental compilation. In a large Rsbuild/Rspack application, editing one watched TSX module triggers a graph-wide Tailwind scan even when the edited module transforms in roughly 28 ms. The CLI already has an incremental `scanFiles` path; using the compiler's changed-file set lets the webpack integration do the same while retaining safe full-scan fallbacks.

An upstream-quality patch against the current source is here (2.5 KB, SHA-256 `f5086ce947eccc2031bf8ae70b81aaf5c72dde41fef26c01090da9128b5b654d`):

available privately

### Proposed behavior

On an incremental rebuild, use `compiler.modifiedFiles` and call `scanner.scanFiles(changedFiles)` only when every changed path is an existing, non-CSS source file and no files were removed. Fall back to the existing full `scanner.scan()` for:

- the initial build or a full rebuild strategy;
- deleted, missing, or directory paths;
- `.css`/`.CSS` edits, which can change Tailwind semantics and should not be treated as source tokens;
- `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, or `.git/info/exclude` edits, which can expose previously ignored sources.

The candidate/build path otherwise stays unchanged: `compiler.build(newCandidates ?? [...context.candidates])`. This mirrors the CLI's incremental strategy and introduces no configuration knobs.

### Measurements

An isolated scanner benchmark with 12,001 TSX source files and eight one-file edits reports:

```text
scanner.scanFiles(changedFiles): median 0.104 ms
scanner.scan():                  median 121.009 ms
speedup:                         about 1,164x
```

The larger application has roughly 417 entries, 5,495 rendered chunks, and 6,002 assets; removing repeated full-source scans is important both for loader time and because the watched dependency lifecycle amplifies downstream Rspack snapshot/graph work.

### Validation

The patch was checked against the published 4.3.1 source (the unmodified source build produced a byte-identical published webpack dist) and the current upstream source. Sixteen isolated loader correctness cases pass with the 4.3.1 Oxide/node packages, including:

```text
existing TSX edit and newly added source
ignored/out-of-root/@source-not files
removed, missing, mixed, and directory paths
.css and .CSS edits
.gitignore, .ignore, and exclude controls
new CSS variable/theme input
16 passed; 0 failed
```

Source/declaration builds, formatting, and patch apply checks are clean. This was uncovered while working with the Rspack team on precise CSS HMR; the related Rspack-side regression and evidence are documented at https://github.com/web-infra-dev/rspack/pull/14682#issuecomment-4961532402 and https://github.com/web-infra-dev/rspack/issues/14765.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "[Bug]: @tailwindcss/webpack fully rescans sources on every one-file HMR rebuild" (#20326)

Issues.Title: Add s390x-unknown-linux-gnu target
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Adds `s390x-unknown-linux-gnu` (Linux on IBM Z, big-endian) as a supported platform for `@tailwindcss/oxide`, so it ships a prebuilt binding like the other Linux targets.

The oxide engine is byte-order-correct on big-endian — no code changes were needed, only build/packaging config:

- Register `s390x-unknown-linux-gnu` in `napi.targets` + add the `@tailwindcss/oxide-linux-s390x-gnu` optional dependency
- Add the `crates/node/npm/linux-s390x-gnu` sub-package
- Add an `s390x-unknown-linux-gnu` row to the release build matrix (cross-compiled via `--use-napi-cross`, so no s390x runner is required)

## Test plan

Verified on a native s390x host (RHEL, GCC 11.5, Node 24):

- `cargo test` → **332 passed, 0 failed** (extractors, scanner, glob, utf16)
- Built the native binding with
  `pnpm run --filter @tailwindcss/oxide build:platform` → `tailwindcss-oxide.linux-s390x-gnu.node`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add s390x-unknown-linux-gnu target" (#20327)

Issues.Title: npm ci fails with Tailwind CSS 4.3.2 due to missing optional dependencies
Issues.Body:
I just ran into a similar issue as #20016 

A `package-lock.json` generated on Windows fails during deploy on Linux in GitHub Actions when using `npm ci`. Switching the GitHub Actions install step from `npm ci` to `npm install` works around it.

**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**
`tailwindcss@4.3.2`
`@tailwindcss/cli@4.3.2`
`@tailwindcss/oxide@4.3.2`

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**
no framework build wrapper - `tailwindcss -i ./src/styles/app.css -o ./public/app.css --minify`
wrangler for deploy/build

**What version of Node.js are you using?**
v24.13.0 npm 11.6.2

**What operating system are you using?**
Windows for dev; failing deploy path in Github Actions runs ubuntu-latest

The exact error:
```
npm error npm ci can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync.
npm error Missing: @emnapi/runtime@1.11.2 from lock file
npm error Missing: @emnapi/core@1.11.2 from lock file
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "npm ci fails with Tailwind CSS 4.3.2 due to missing optional dependencies" (#20324)

Issues.Title: Lazy load `@parcel/watcher`
Issues.Body: This PR ensure that we lazy load the `@parcel/watcher` in the `@tailwindcss/cli`. This means that we don't have to load it at all when using a normal build or when using `--watch --poll` combination. The bigger reason is that on some platforms `@parcel/watcher` might not work, and therefore the build will fail even if you don't use `--watch` at all. This PR fixes that by lazy loading it. Then, if we can't load it when using `--watch`, a useful workaround is shown by using `--watch --poll` instead. This PR also improves showing errors such that the `error.cause` property can be rendered as well. Maybe in the future we can make use of deferred imports (https://github.com/tc39/proposal-defer-import-eval) Fixes: #20322 ## Test plan 1. All tests still pass [ci-all] 2. Fabricated a fake error locally to prove that we can still use a normal build and `--watch --poll` as a workaround
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Lazy load `@parcel/watcher`" (#20325)
